apiKeys.heading: Get an API key
apiKeys.intro: ExtrAct uses OpenAI's or Anthropic's AI to transcribe your documents. You'll need to create an account with one of these providers and paste your personal key into <bold>Settings > AI</bold>.
apiKeys.privacyNote: Your key is stored <bold>only on your computer</bold>. ExtrAct never sends it anywhere except to the provider you picked, at transcription time.

anthropic.title: Anthropic (Claude)
steps: Click <bold>Open the console</bold> and create an account (or sign in).
Verify your email then your phone number.
Under Plans & Billing, add a few dollars of credit.
Copy the key (it starts with sk-ant-) and paste it into Settings > AI.

openai.title: OpenAI (GPT)
steps: Click <bold>Open the platform</bold> and create an account (or sign in).
Under Billing, add a few dollars of credit.
Under API keys, click Create new secret key.
Copy the key (it starts with sk-) and paste it into Settings > AI.
openai.footnote: The key is shown only once — copy it before closing the window.

workflow.heading: How does it work?
workflow.intro: ExtrAct turns your PDFs (newspapers, magazines, correspondence…) into structured items via AI. Here are the main steps.

steps.title: 1. Create a project
steps.body: From All projects, click New project, give it a name, and choose a default template (Press article, Correspondence, or a custom one). A project can hold several PDFs (the sources) and several folders to organise them.

steps.title: 2. Import one or more sources
steps.body: In the Sources tab, import your PDFs (or JPG/PNG images, which will be converted). Each source becomes a clickable thumbnail. The gear button lets you rename, download, or replace a source's PDF.

steps.title: 3. Extract items
steps.body: Click a source to open the Extraction page. Draw a rectangle around each article / letter / ad. Multiple zones can belong to the same item if it spans columns or pages. Save keeps your work in progress as a draft; Generate produces the PDF for each item and files it in the chosen folder.

steps.title: 4. Transcribe in the editor
steps.body: Click an item (or tick several then Transcribe) to open the editor. The AI transcription fills the template fields automatically. You can then correct by hand, navigate between items with the arrows, and apply a different template if needed.

steps.title: 5. Organise
steps.body: In the Items tab, drag and drop articles to reorder them or move them between folders. Select several (checkbox) for bulk actions: move, export, delete. The Incomplete only filter shows just the items whose fields aren't all filled in.

steps.title: 6. Export
steps.body: Export one, several, or all items as PDF, DOCX, TXT, or PNG. Each exported item is accompanied by its source and original page number. The whole project can also be exported as a ZIP backup.

steps.title: 7. Search
steps.body: The Search page looks up a word or phrase across every project, all fields combined. Search is accent- and case-insensitive. You can filter by project / folder / template / field, and export the matched results (with the search term highlighted in DOCX and PDF).

models.heading: Which model should I pick?
models.intro: ExtrAct supports two AI model families. You can configure both and switch any time from <bold>Settings > AI</bold>.

anthropic.title: Anthropic — Claude
anthropic.intro: Usually more accurate on old documents, handwriting, and complex layouts.
items: <bold>Haiku 4.5</bold> — fast and cheap, enough for clean text.
<bold>Opus 4.7</bold> — the most accurate, for tough documents.

openai.title: OpenAI — GPT
openai.intro: Often faster and a bit cheaper at similar quality.
items: <bold>GPT-5.5</bold> — premium model, for the most demanding cases.

costs.title: How much does it cost?
costs.body: Cost depends on the model and document length. Count a few cents for a short item with an economy model, up to ten cents for a long document with a premium one. <bold>Settings > Logs</bold> shows the actual cumulative cost of each of your transcriptions.

templatesSection.heading: Templates
templatesSection.intro: A <bold>template</bold> defines the structure of the information to extract: which fields to fill, their type, and how to guide the AI.

defaults.title: Default templates
defaults.footnote: These templates can't be modified, but you can duplicate them from the Templates page.

custom.title: Create a custom template
steps: Go to <bold>Templates</bold> in the left menu.
Click <bold>New template</bold> and give it a name.
Add your fields. Three types are available:
Optional: add an AI hint to guide the transcription (e.g. "Keep the document's original spelling").
Save. Your template will appear when creating a project.
custom.footnote: The <bold>Title</bold> field is always present and can't be removed.
